draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Dharmasthala! The big temple here is a real one-off: a Shiva temple run by a Jain family, with Vaishnava Madhwa Brahmins doing the poojas.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat here, so ask around near the temple for a simple meal.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Manjusha Museum is a 2 min walk, Dharmasthala Temple is about 3 minutes away, and the Bahubali Statue is an 8 min walk.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Wander over to Lalithodyana Park for a slow, quiet break from the temple crowds.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Besides Shiva as Manjunatha, the temple also honours the Jain Tirthankara Chandraprabha and four guardian spirits of Dharma.

spots.name: Manjusha Museum
spots.detail: 2 min walk · Antiques, paintings and temple chariots from across Karnataka

spots.name: Dharmasthala Temple
spots.detail: 3 min walk · The 800-year-old Hindu-Jain temple to Manjunatha

spots.name: Bahubali Statue
spots.detail: 8 min walk · A big statue of Bahubali close to the temple

legends.title: The guardians of Dharma
legends.body: Alongside Manjunatha and Ammanavaru, the temple has shrines to the Dharma Daivas, guardian spirits named Kalarahu, Kalarkayi, Kumaraswamy and Kanyakumari. Locals see them as the protectors of the place.

tips.title: Come early.
tips.body: Around 2,000 pilgrims visit the temple on an average day, so mornings are calmer.

tips.title: Do both museums.
tips.body: Next to the Manjusha Museum there's the Manjusha Car Museum, full of vintage cars from the same founder.

story.title: Kuduma by the river
story.body: Before it was Dharmasthala, the town on the banks of the Nethravathi was known as Kuduma. Its temple has stood here for about 800 years.

story.title: A temple reconsecrated
story.body: In the 16th century the Dvaita saint Vadiraja Tirtha reconsecrated the temple. He did it at the request of the administrator of the time, Devaraja Heggade.

story.title: Jain hands, Hindu rites
story.body: The administration stayed with a Jain Bunt family called the Pergades, while Madhwa Brahmin priests run the rituals. That mix is what makes the temple so unusual.

story.title: Temple and treasures
story.body: Temple head Veerendra Heggade founded the Manjusha Museum just south of the temple. It holds antiques, temple chariots and vintage cars gathered from across Karnataka.
